query: What clinical study design parameters must be prespecified for regulatory acceptance: sample size/power calculations, site/operator stratification, prospective capture of invalid/indeterminate rates, and turnaround time metrics?

response.query: What clinical study design parameters must be prespecified for regulatory acceptance: sample size/power calculations, site/operator stratification, prospective capture of invalid/indeterminate rates, and turnaround time metrics?
response.answer: For regulatory acceptance, clinical study design must prespecify sample size/power calculations, site/operator stratification, and turnaround time metrics. Invalid/indeterminate rates should also be captured prospectively.

results.title: 21 CFR Part 866 -- Immunology and Microbiology Devices - eCFR
results.content: (1) The intended use for the device in the labeling required under § 809.10 of this chapter must include a detailed description of the targets the device detects, the type of results provided to the user, the clinical indications appropriate for test use, and the specific population(s) for which the device is intended. (iv) Detailed discussion of the performance characteristics of the device observed in a clinical study performed on a population that is consistent with the intended use population in comparison to the results obtained by a reference or comparator method determined to be acceptable by FDA, for microbial detection, identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing; and. (iii) A description of applicable test limitations, including, for device specific mutations validated with method comparison data to a medically established test in the same intended specimen type, appropriate description of the level of evidence and/or the differences between next generation sequencing results and results from the medically established test (*e.g.,* as described in professional guidelines).
